To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed Kd-networks are a competitive approach for shape recognition tasks and can be used as an alternative to the currently dominant convolution based architectures.

(1) Kd-networks outperform the current state-of-the-art methods on the SHREC 2014 shape part segmentation benchmark; (2) Kd-network outperforms the current state-ofthe-art methods on the Princeton Shape Benchmark (PSB) and ModelNet40 shape recognition benchmarks; and (3) Kd-network performs on par with state-of-the-art deep convolutional networks on the ModelNet40 benchmark.

Kd-networks: (1) are a new type of deep learning architecture that is designed for point cloud processing, (2) perform multiplicative transformations, (3) share parameters of these transformations, (4) are not based on any rasterization, (5) are competitive with the state of the art in 3D model classification, 3D model retrieval and shape part recognition.

the following questions. How can we design a new deep learning network that is suitable for the recognition of 3D point clouds? How does the new architecture compare to other architectures in terms of accuracy and efficiency? What is the best way to use Kd-networks for shape recognition tasks?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Kd-networks outperform all other deep architectures in shape classification tasks and are competitive in shape part segmentation and retrieval tasks, while requiring much less training time and memory.
Kd-networks are a promising alternative to the currently dominant convolution-based architectures for the recognition of 3D point clouds.

Kd-networks are the first deep learning models that are designed for 3-D shape recognition and work with unstructured 3-D point clouds, and that they are competitive with the current state of the art.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an end-to-end trainable deep learning architecture for 3D point cloud recognition tasks.

we present a novel architecture for deep learning with point cloud data that is competitive in a number of tasks, while at the same time avoiding the poor scaling behavior of the dominant convolutional architectures.
the Kd-networks are the first deep neural networks for point clouds that can be trained with a reasonable number of training data points and that scale well to large point clouds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Kd-networks are able to perform well on 3D point clouds, which is an unstructured data type.

the new architecture can be successfully applied to the problem of point cloud processing, and that it can be a viable alternative to the existing convolutional architectures in the context of 3D model processing.

the new architecture can be used to design efficient deep neural networks for 3D data that are not limited to the uniform grid structures and can therefore avoid the problems with poor scalability and memory consumption that are common for such grids.
